CT CORONARY ANGIOGRAPHY

Clinical details: 71-year-old man. Exertional chest tightness and breathlessness, worsening over 6 weeks. Permanent atrial fibrillation, rate controlled. Apixaban.

Technique:
Non-contrast prospectively gated calcium score acquisition followed by prospectively ECG-triggered CT coronary angiography.
Heart rate 66 bpm, atrial fibrillation. Metoprolol 15 mg IV. GTN 800 micrograms sublingual.
Contrast: Omnipaque 350, 70 ml.
DLP 312 mGy.cm (estimated effective dose 8.1 mSv).

Calcium score:
Total Agatston score 688 (LMS 38, LAD 402, LCx 21, RCA 227). 79th percentile for age, sex and ethnicity (MESA).

Coronary arteries:
Right dominant.
Normal coronary origins and course.
Mild motion artefact at the mid RCA; diagnostic.
LMS: calcified plaque with minimal (1-24%) stenosis.
LAD: mixed plaque in the proximal segment with severe (70-99%) stenosis. High-risk plaque features: positive remodelling and low-attenuation plaque. First diagonal: minimal (1-24%) ostial stenosis.
LCx: calcified plaque in the proximal segment with minimal (1-24%) stenosis. Obtuse marginals unremarkable.
RCA: mixed plaque in the mid segment with moderate (50-69%) stenosis. No high-risk plaque features.
No myocardial bridging.

Non-coronary findings:
Left atrium dilated. Other cardiac chambers normal in size. No pericardial effusion.
There is incomplete opacification of the left atrial appendage tip, likely mixing artefact in this single arterial phase acquisition; thrombus cannot be excluded.
Ascending aorta 37 mm. Pulmonary trunk 26 mm.
Visualised lung bases unremarkable. No significant extracardiac findings.

Conclusion:
1. Severe (70-99%) proximal LAD stenosis in mixed plaque with high-risk features. Moderate (50-69%) mid RCA stenosis. CAD-RADS 4A/P3/HRP.
2. Referral for invasive coronary angiography is recommended.
3. Thrombus in the left atrial appendage cannot be excluded; transoesophageal echocardiography is advised before any cardioversion.
4. Optimisation of preventive therapy and risk factor modification is advised.
